note.text: An environmental discussion should connect a specific action to its purpose. Reducing waste prevents some waste at source; reusing gives an appropriate object another use; recycling requires a suitable treatment route. Sorting alone does not prove a material is recycled. Use the school’s actual instructions for practical work and keep unknown or dangerous waste outside pupils’ handling tasks. This lesson practises language through fictional proposals rather than arranging an unsupervised activity.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to support a proposal with a reason and a practical limit in a prepared discussion. Builds on: reading natural-resource proposals and writing explanations. Leads to: air-pollution listening preparation and careful conclusions.

sections.heading: Read the original model
sections.text: Original dialogue: Bih proposes avoiding unnecessary printing. Ayuk suggests reusing a clean box for materials. Another member asks which materials the local collection arrangement accepts. The group will check the teacher’s instructions before acting. Each proposal explains a possible benefit without claiming that one small action solves every environmental problem.

sections.heading: Apply and check
sections.text: Prepare short turns: state the point, give a relevant reason and invite a response. Use fictional people if the subject is private. Practise with a partner when available; written choices here do not establish oral fluency or listening ability. Challenge an idea without insulting the speaker.

cards.idea: A correction must preserve the intended meaning and form.
example: Reduction necessarily means producing more waste. Correction: The aim is to prevent part of the use or waste.
Every reuse requires industrial material transformation. Correction: The object can remain intact while its use changes.
Sorting any object guarantees it has already been recycled. Correction: Collection, sorting and actual processing are different stages.
A good proposal must claim it solves every problem instantly. Correction: Specific conditions make a proposal more realistic.
